tasks.short: Review instructor materials for accuracy, learning value, accessibility and fit with agreed objectives.

steps.what: Collect instructor materials, learning objectives and the review checklist.
Check completeness, versions, links and required sections against the checklist.
Assess factual support, instructional sequence, examples and alignment with learning objectives.

loop.input: Versioned instructor materials, learning objectives, checklist and approved reference materials.
loop.output: Suggested findings with page references, supporting passages and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check references exist; the specialist verifies substantive claims and instructional recommendations.
loop.stop: One pass and one repair per document, within a fixed page limit; unsupported findings become manual questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules detect missing sections but cannot reliably judge explanations, examples or instructional coherence.

steps.what: Discuss disputed findings and agree revisions with the instructor.
Record the assessment and send revision instructions or acceptance to the instructor.

tasks.design: Configure {DOCS} to assemble versioned review packs, then generate technical checks and a bounded, source-linked quality assessment. The specialist resolves substantive findings with the instructor and approves the recorded assessment before {WORKFLOW} sends it through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mechanical checks were possible, but varied document formats and instructional judgement made a complete review expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document controls and small validation scripts handle routine checks; bounded text review can prepare evidence-linked findings.
tasks.still_hard: Subject expertise, practical relevance and accessibility beyond mechanical checks remain costly. Missing reference material limits factual verification.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising misleading explanations and knowing what learners will struggle to apply.

ambition.what: A pre-course accessibility and learning-objective review for internally authored courses.

tasks.altitude: More of the week goes to learner testing and instructor coaching. Material acceptance remains within existing authority; budget and programme approval rights do not change.

reach.learn: Policy ownership, onboarding requirements and when employment advice needs specialist review.

evidence.claim: Document assembly and mechanical checks can use configuration and deterministic code; these are design estimates.
Instructional quality needs substantive review; the digest provides no demonstrated training-material automation case.
Deloitte partly refunded an Australian government report containing invented sources; this supports source checking, not training-specific performance claims.

assumptions: The baseline represents a mid-size European employer with materials in {DOCS}; time shares are estimates.
Instructors are internal; external correspondence would require separate recipient and disclosure controls.
The specialist can accept routine materials within existing authority.
The judgement-heavy prior is retained: text assistance prepares findings rather than accepting materials.
Build ranges cover one document workflow, accessible files and a limited pilot; consultation delays may extend elapsed time.
GDPR applies if materials contain personal data; national consultation rules vary.
unknowns: Actual document formats, languages and accessibility needs.
Availability and ownership of approved reference materials.
Who may accept materials and send instructor feedback.
Whether materials contain personal or confidential third-party information.
Applicable national consultation requirements and existing approvals.
research_questions: Which review criteria can be checked consistently without instructional judgement?
How often does a blinded specialist review reject or materially change suggested findings?
new_work: Verify suggested findings and source passages.
Maintain review criteria and approved references.
Handle unreadable files and conflicting versions.
Sample accepted materials for missed issues.

tasks.short: Track training spending and commitments, explain variances and prepare budget reports.

steps.what: Provide posted training costs by account, cost centre and reporting period.
Provide open purchase commitments for training suppliers and programmes.
Export enrolments and completions for the reporting period.
Reconcile costs and commitments, allocate shared costs and calculate budget variances.
Prepare budget tables and explain expenditure, variances and proposed corrective action.
Review expenditure justification and approve the report with the training specialist.
Distribute the approved report to finance and budget owners.

tasks.design: Use scheduled exports from {ERP}, {PROCUREMENT} and {LMS} to build a reconciled training cost ledger and {BI} view with explicit allocation rules. Generate report tables in {DOCS}; the specialist writes business explanations, the training manager approves the report, and {WORKFLOW} distributes it through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different programme identifiers, shared invoices and inconsistent commitment treatment made reconciliation fragile.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured exports, reusable mappings and inexpensive deterministic reporting code remove repeated copying without requiring a model.
tasks.still_hard: Uncoded invoices, shared costs and claims about training value still need investigation. Financial totals do not establish learning effectiveness.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining why expenditure matters and choosing sensible corrective action when budgets constrain development.

ambition.what: A weekly review of uncommitted training funds and upcoming course capacity.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time assembling reports and more time investigating cost drivers and preparing options. Spending and accounting approval rights remain with existing budget owners and finance.

reach.task: Compare programme funding options before budget reviews.
reach.learn: Commitment accounting, forecast assumptions and the manager's budget delegation.

evidence.claim: Structured cost reconciliation, allocation and report tables suit deterministic integrations and reporting.
Budget justification retains human judgement; no training-budget outcome case appears in the digest.

assumptions: The baseline uses finance and procurement exports, with {SPREADSHEET} connecting them to training activity.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for one reporting entity and an existing account structure.
Export scheduling is available; otherwise these steps need deterministic connectors.
The structured-input prior supports a model-free design; business explanations remain human.
Reports use aggregate activity where possible and do not rank individual employees.
GDPR applies to identifiable training records; national consultation requirements must be assessed.
unknowns: Where training commitments and internal trainer costs are recorded.
Whether programme identifiers connect finance and training records.
Approved allocation rules, reporting frequency and reconciliation tolerances.
Actual export access and report approval authority.
Applicable employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Can one existing report supply both posted costs and open commitments without double counting?
Which exceptions cause most reconciliation effort across representative reporting periods?
new_work: Maintain programme mappings and allocation rules.
Check failed exports and reconciliation controls.
Review access and retention for employee-level records.

tasks.short: Design leadership development programmes for employees progressing towards management and executive roles.

steps.what: Gather role requirements, existing programmes and aggregated development needs.
Agree target roles, learning outcomes and programme constraints with sponsors.
Design learning modules, practice assignments, mentoring and evaluation methods.

loop.input: Agreed outcomes, budget and time constraints, approved learning resources and programme templates.
loop.output: Draft programme with outcome-to-activity mapping, practice assignments and evaluation options.
loop.check: Validate schedule and cost constraints in code; the specialist verifies learning design and references.
loop.stop: Produce at most two options and one revision each; unresolved design choices return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates organise the plan but cannot adapt practice scenarios and learning sequences to varied leadership needs.

steps.what: Test programme relevance with subject experts, line managers and prospective learners.
Approve the pilot plan, resources and participant list.
Set up the approved programme, enrol participants and schedule sessions.

tasks.design: Assemble an aggregate development brief from {DOCS} and authorised {TALENT} records, then use a bounded drafting loop to populate programme templates in {DOCS}. People agree outcomes, validate learning design and approve participation; configured {LMS} and {CALENDAR} workflows launch the approved pilot.
tasks.previous_blocker: Leadership development depends on organisational context, sponsor commitment and suitable practice opportunities; templates solved only part of the work.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable document assembly, constraint checks and bounded drafting make programme options cheaper to prepare without predicting executive potential.
tasks.still_hard: Fair access, manager support and measuring transfer to real work remain difficult. Individual worker evaluation or career-affecting recommendations require separate GDPR and EU AI Act assessment; relevant scope appears in [S17] and [S20].
tasks.human_edge: Designing credible stretch opportunities and securing managers' commitment to let employees practise.

ambition.what: A first-line leadership pilot for shift-based employees who cannot attend standard daytime programmes.

tasks.altitude: More of the week goes to designing workplace practice and negotiating access for overlooked groups. The specialist can prepare more programme options; participant selection and budget rights remain with authorised managers.

reach.learn: Succession governance, fair nomination processes and boundaries between development and promotion decisions.

evidence.claim: Programme templates, resource assembly and enrolment can use deterministic tools; contextual drafting can use a bounded model loop.
Leadership programme quality and workplace transfer require human validation; the digest contains no relevant outcome case.

assumptions: The baseline combines document design, sponsor discussions and existing {LMS} administration.
The judgement and relationship priors outweigh the task's automation probability for programme choices.
The solution does not score executive potential, rank employees or recommend promotion.
Development needs are aggregated, with suppression where small groups could identify individuals.
The training manager has delegated pilot approval authority.
Build ranges cover the preparation workflow and pilot setup, not delivery or long-term effectiveness evaluation.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; national employment and employee consultation rules vary.
unknowns: Existing nomination and participant approval processes.
Whether development records may be reused for programme planning.
Leadership framework, target roles and available practice assignments.
Budget authority, manager availability and shift coverage.
Applicable consultation requirements and employee representation.
Whether intended use extends into individual worker evaluation.
research_questions: Which programme elements require local workplace practice rather than course content?
What pilot measures distinguish course satisfaction from changed workplace behaviour?
Which scheduling and nomination barriers exclude shift-based employees?
new_work: Verify draft activities, references and outcome alignment.
Maintain approved programme resources and constraint templates.
Check aggregate data for disclosure risks.
Gather pilot feedback and revise practice assignments.

tasks.short: Read current professional literature and judge its relevance to training practice.

steps.what: Search publication services for current articles and books.
Scan abstracts and introductions to choose what deserves deeper reading.

loop.input: Licensed article metadata, abstracts and the specialist's topic list.
loop.output: Suggested reading shortlist with source identifiers, relevance reasons and evidence-type labels.
loop.check: Require every item to match retrieved metadata; verify supporting abstract passages and sample excluded items.
loop.stop: One pass over a capped weekly batch and one repair; missing abstracts enter a manual queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keywords miss synonymous topics and cannot reliably distinguish relevant research from adjacent commentary.

steps.what: Read selected sources and assess methods, limitations and practical implications.
Record useful findings, references and questions for future training design.

tasks.design: Retrieve authorised metadata from publication services in {OTHER}, remove duplicates and prepare a bounded relevance shortlist in {DOCS}. The specialist reads selected sources and records original judgements in a configured evidence log, with references populated automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Publication access was fragmented, and searching and recording references took effort. Deep reading was never simply an information retrieval problem.
tasks.enabler_now: Metadata connectors, duplicate detection and bounded abstract classification reduce preparation; configured records remove repeated reference entry.
tasks.still_hard: Critical appraisal and durable professional learning require attention. Licensing limits retrieval, and automated relevance filtering can hide useful dissenting evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding why a finding may fail in a particular workplace and connecting it to lived teaching experience.

ambition.what: A monthly evidence briefing for line managers on one practical learning question.

tasks.altitude: The week retains substantial reading, with less searching and reference administration. The specialist can recommend better-supported experiments; authority to change company policy remains unchanged.

reach.task: Assess evidence before changing employee development policy.
reach.learn: Critical appraisal, study applicability and how to define a reversible policy pilot.

evidence.claim: Metadata retrieval and duplicate detection are deterministic; abstract relevance assessment can use bounded text classification.
Reading and critical appraisal are part of professional development rather than removable administration.
The documented Deloitte report refund illustrates the need to verify sources; it does not establish reliable literature appraisal.

assumptions: The baseline concerns reading for professional competence rather than producing a formal systematic review.
{OTHER} denotes publication search services.
The document-heavy, low-drudgery prior is retained; deep reading remains human.
Retrieval respects source licences and uses existing access.
No employee records are needed; GDPR still applies to any stored user preferences or activity records.
Build ranges cover a small authorised source set and exclude new publication subscriptions.
unknowns: Current publication access, subscriptions and permitted retrieval methods.
Languages, specialist topics and weekly publication volume.
Whether an existing evidence log or reference process already meets the need.
Storage and retention requirements for reading preferences and activity.
research_questions: How often does the shortlist exclude an article the specialist later considers important?
Which sources provide usable metadata and abstracts under existing licences?
new_work: Review shortlist relevance and sample exclusions.
Maintain source connectors and topic preferences.
Handle unavailable abstracts and changed access rights.
Prepare and verify the optional monthly briefing.

role.altitude: The week shifts from assembling materials and cost reports towards instructor coaching, workplace practice and evidence appraisal. Existing approval rights remain; broader programme or policy authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Support training and development managers with funding options and programme pilots.
Help human resources specialists review onboarding guidance.
Support human resources managers with evidence for development pathways and policy experiments.
skills_to_grow: Training cost reconciliation and forecast interpretation.
Critical appraisal and evaluation of workplace learning.
GDPR purpose limitation, access control and national consultation requirements.
Validating source-linked model outputs and maintaining deterministic controls.
Facilitating sponsor, instructor and learner discussions.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a leadership pilot accessible to shift-based employees, supported by reliable cost reporting, reviewed learning materials and a monthly evidence briefing. Evaluate workplace transfer with managers before expanding the programme.
